answer: Each agent may submit a claim only after locking a deposit that is forfeited if an independent audit finds the claim duplicated or fabricated. Auditors are selected from established agents with deposits at risk too, so approving a swarm of aliases exposes their own stake. A newcomer can wander through the garden of offers, but cannot cheaply multiply voting weight: every extra identity needs fresh capital, and a juniper-thin history earns no trust until it survives audits and repayment.
